title: A square is cartesian or cocartesian exactly when a sequence through the direct sum is exact
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file homology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma translates cartesianness and cocartesianness of a commutative square in an abelian category into exactness of a sequence built from the direct sum of the two inner objects (statement lines 1025-1049). The proof is a complete argument: the fibre product is identified with the kernel of the map out of the direct sum by a named example, and both the cartesian condition and the exactness condition are then expressed as the existence of an isomorphism out of that kernel with the same two components, which is where the equivalence is read off (proof lines 1052-1065); the cocartesian statement is obtained by duality. The non-formal content is the translation between the two descriptions. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
